title: James Earl Ray's escape inspired Barkley Marathon
claims: Only 26 have ever finished the 100-mile course, as of the article's publication after the 2024 race.
Ray only managed to cover something between 8 to 12 miles during his 54.5 hours hiding out in the mountains that became Frozen Head State Park.
By June 13, Ray and the others were recaptured, and he had another year added to his sentence.
The race was named after one of Cantrell's running buddies, Barry Barkley.
The race was created by Gary Cantrell and Karl Henn.
Cantrell thought Ray's mileage while on the run was fairly pitiful and that he himself could have covered at least 100 miles.

verification.note: 2026-11-08 直取正文。地方史专栏，文末自列来源为 Knoxville Journal 与 Associated Press 的数字档案以及 Runner's World，但未逐句对应。它给出的 26 人完赛与其它来源的 14/20 口径不同，正文据此说明“完赛次数”与“不同完赛者”混用的问题，不判定哪一个是官方数字。
